insights.headline: Gold slips for a fourth session as oil-driven inflation fears cement December Fed hike bets
insights.summary: Gold eased for a fourth straight session on Wednesday, with spot near $4,118 an ounce, as higher crude prices revived inflation worries and pushed December Fed rate-hike odds to 90%. Silver fell 0.9% to $57.44. Offsetting the gloom, an NDB Wealth report sees gold holding $4,200-5,000 over 12-24 months as central banks and Asian buyers increasingly drive prices, while India's festive demand is showing early strength with domestic discounts narrowing to $8 an ounce.
points: Spot gold down 0.2% at $4,118; December US gold futures at $4,136 as the oil rally reinforces hawkish Fed expectations.
Traders price a 90% chance of a December Fed hike versus 16% for Oct 27-28.
NDB Wealth sees $4,200-5,000 gold over 12-24 months in its 50% base case, driven by central-bank and Asian demand.
India's gold discounts narrowed to $8/oz from $66 in September as festive demand picked up, the World Gold Council says.
Russia's central bank has sold about 62 tonnes of gold since December 2025, its biggest reserve drawdown since 1998.

trending.title: Fed vs oil: the tug-of-war capping gold
trending.summary: A fourth daily decline shows how Middle East oil risks cut both ways for gold: higher crude lifts inflation fears, which keep Fed hike bets - now 90% for December - firmly in place.

trending.title: Central banks rewrite gold's playbook
trending.summary: 'Gold has stopped trading off the Fed,' NDB Wealth argues, citing 289t of Q2 official buying and record Asian fund inflows; Russia's 62t sell-off to fund its deficit is the structural exception.

trending.title: India's festive season starts on a firmer footing
trending.summary: Domestic discounts have collapsed to $8/oz, ETF inflows ran hot in September, and jewellers report improving footfall - though high prices push buyers toward lighter pieces and old-gold exchange.

trending.title: Silver's 2026 balance sheet is still contested
trending.summary: Deutsche Bank and StoneX are talking surplus, but the Silver Institute still projects a 46.3 Moz deficit for a sixth straight year - and even the deficit case assumes solar demand falls 19%.

items.title: Gold dips for fourth session as oil rally fans inflation concerns
items.summary: Gold fell for a fourth straight session as oil prices stoked inflation fears. Spot gold slipped 0.2% to $4,118 an ounce; December gold futures eased 0.2% to $4,136.20. Reuters-polled economists expect the Fed to skip a hike in October and raise rates in December - CME FedWatch puts December odds at 90% versus 16% for October 27-28. Spot silver fell 0.9% to $57.44.

items.title: Gold may trade up to USD 5,000/oz over next two years as central banks sustain demand: Report
items.summary: Gold could hold $4,200-5,000 an ounce over the next 12-24 months, NDB Wealth Management said in an ANI-carried report, as central-bank buying and Asian investor demand increasingly set prices rather than US rates. It cites 289 tonnes of central-bank buying in Q2 2026 and record Asian gold-fund inflows of nearly 70 tonnes in H1; the $4,200-5,000 range is its 50%-probability base case.

items.title: World Gold Council: India's seasonal gold demand shows early strength
items.summary: Domestic discounts narrowed from an average of $66 an ounce in September to $8 as of October 16, the World Gold Council says, as seasonal demand gathered pace. September gold ETF inflows hit a seven-month high of Rs 44.5 billion (about 3 tonnes), with Rs 17.22 billion (1.2 tonnes) more in the first half of October. September imports fell to $1.8 billion, the lowest since March 2024.

items.title: Russia sells 62 tonnes of gold in biggest reserve drawdown since 1998
items.summary: Bank of Russia data show gold reserves fell another 200,000 troy ounces (6.2 tonnes) in September, to 72.8 million ounces (2,264 tonnes) — the lowest since end-2019. The central bank has cut holdings for ten straight months, disposing of about 62 tonnes since December 2025, as the Kremlin covers a widening budget deficit; the Finance Ministry expects the 2026 deficit to reach 7.3 trillion roubles.

items.title: Silver Surplus Calls May Overstate the Impact of Weaker Solar Demand
items.summary: Deutsche Bank and StoneX have shifted to surplus language - a possible physical silver surplus in 2027, or a 2026 surplus of about five weeks of demand (~107 Moz). Przemyslaw Radomski argues the solar decline is largely already counted: Metals Focus and the Silver Institute already assume PV demand falls 19% to 151 Moz inside a 46.3 Moz 2026 shortfall.

items.title: CIBC slashes gold price forecasts, still sees $5,500 in 2028
items.summary: In its October outlook, CIBC cut its Q4 2026 gold forecast to $4,500 an ounce from $6,500, its 2027 average to $5,200 from $6,500 and its 2028 estimate to $5,500 from $6,000. The bank cites higher energy prices, a stronger dollar and a more hawkish Fed; it also cut its 2027 silver forecast to $85 an ounce from $120.

items.title: Gem, jewellery exporters heave a sigh of relief as the US puts off punitive tax
items.summary: Indian gem and jewellery exporters expect US orders to revive after President Trump waived proposed 100% punitive duties on goods from top Russian oil buyers. The US remains India's largest export market ahead of Christmas demand, and industry exports rose 13% to $14.30 billion in the fiscal first half. IBJA data showed domestic gold fell 5% in the past month to Rs 145,944 per 10 grams.

items.title: Hindustan Zinc Q2 profit more than doubles on higher metal prices; silver output up 20%
items.summary: Hindustan Zinc's consolidated net profit more than doubled to Rs 6,412 crore in Q2 FY27 as higher metal prices and record output lifted revenue 76.5% to Rs 15,093 crore, margin widening to 42%. Silver production rose 20% to 173 tonnes and silver sales revenue more than doubled, driving about 45% of profitability; Jefferies said firmer silver prices improved the profit outlook.

items.title: RBI sets SGB 2020-21 Series VII redemption at Rs 14,614 for October 19
items.summary: The RBI has fixed October 19, 2026 as the premature redemption date for Sovereign Gold Bond 2020-21 Series VII at Rs 14,614 per gram, based on IBJA's average closing prices of October 14-16. Online subscribers gain 192.22% and offline buyers 189.33% in capital gains, alongside 2.5% annual interest; holders must route requests through their receiving offices within the notification window.

items.title: India's festive and wedding season demand picks up as prices ease
items.summary: Jewellers report improving footfall as the festive and wedding season begins, with manufacturers seeing strong orders and buyers favouring lighter designs and old-gold exchange deals, which rose over 10%. Gold slipped about 5% in India in September, and listed jewellers posted 20-30% revenue growth in the July-September quarter.
